note: Written by Claude from web research; check details before booking. Okayama items drop off after 3 Oct, other Japan items after 9 Oct.

items.title: Ben Howard at People Festival
items.summary: His only listed date right now, and the last stop of the current run. A two-day festival in the old East German broadcasting house on the Spree.

items.title: Under One Sky: 400 years of Japanese art
items.summary: Deities, people and animals in Japanese art, in Ando's concrete-and-glass building at Insel Hombroich; Alexandra Bircken's 'Silver Lining' opens the same day. The museum is closed until 10 Oct for installation. About 2.5 hours from Den Haag.
items.why: Ando architecture, Japanese art, art in landscape

items.title: Sabine Marcelis: Continuum
items.summary: The Rotterdam designer's intervention in Rem Koolhaas's building itself: light, colour and material working with the architecture.
items.why: Light and space, art with architecture

items.title: Benedikte Bjerre: When the wind blows
items.summary: A playful, interactive installation of helium-filled sculptures that drift and gather. Combine with Continuum in one visit.

items.title: Base Line
items.summary: Thematic show in Berlage's building. Worth pairing with the Mondrian rooms on a rainy, windless day.

items.title: Tokyo Atlas
items.summary: International outdoor exhibition placing contemporary art in waterfront parks and public space, including monumental installations.

items.title: Invisible Garden
items.summary: Embroidered landscapes and transparent cell-like sculptures that shimmer and dissolve as you move. Small, quiet, free.

items.title: Rokko Meets Art
items.summary: Site-specific art on Mt Rokko, including works at Tadao Ando's Chapel of the Wind (10:00–16:50) and the Tenran Observatory. Closest thing to the Murou Art Forest feeling near Osaka.
items.why: Ando, art in forest, land art

items.title: Happy Food & Health
items.summary: 100% gluten-free kitchen with vegan dishes, so dairy- and egg-free choices are easy. Ask about oats.

items.title: Sabor Sabor
items.summary: Latin cantina with an open kitchen where the whole menu is gluten-free. Not dairy-free by default, so ask which dishes skip cheese and cream.

items.title: The SUE Store
items.summary: Everything is gluten-free and vegan, so no dairy or eggs. Brunch-style menu; plant milks may include oat, so ask for another.

items.title: Mammamia
items.summary: Rated 4.7, praised by coeliac guests for its gluten-free pizza. Cheese is standard, so order without and check the dough for egg.

items.title: THE SECONDROOM
items.summary: Rated 4.6. Fully vegan and gluten-free, so okonomiyaki, takoyaki and gyoza are all safe from gluten, dairy and egg. Closed Wednesdays.

items.title: Buddha (gluten-free & vegan)
items.summary: Rated 4.7. Gluten-free and vegan, and guests with dairy and egg allergies say they felt safe. Bowls, soups, tacos. Lunch only, closed Sundays.

items.title: FOLK cafe + bakery
items.summary: Rated 5.0. Vegan bakery-café with gluten-free options and a seasonal menu. Not all of it is gluten-free, so ask which bakes are.

items.title: Dune: Part Three in cinemas
items.summary: Denis Villeneuve, who made Arrival, closes his Dune trilogy with Dune Messiah. Dutch release 16 December; worth an IMAX screen.

items.title: Pick: Perfect Days (Wim Wenders, 2023)
items.summary: A Tokyo toilet cleaner's quiet, repeated days, shot like a meditation. Especially good while you're in Japan.

items.title: Pick: The Ministry for the Future (Kim Stanley Robinson)
items.summary: Idea-driven science fiction where the plot is climate finance and adaptation: carbon coins, central banks, heat waves. Chiang-level thinking, aimed at your day job.

items.title: Pick: The Mountain Shadow (Gregory David Roberts)
items.summary: The sequel to Shantaram: Lin back in Bombay two years later, heavier on philosophy. If you haven't read it yet.

items.title: Pick: The Dispossessed (Ursula K. Le Guin)
items.summary: A physicist moves between two worlds and two economic systems. Like Chiang, it is really about how an idea reshapes a life.

items.title: Pick: Wheels of Life (Anodea Judith)
items.summary: The practical companion to Eastern Body, Western Mind: the chakra system as an embodied practice rather than theory.

items.title: Zen silent retreat, autumn
items.summary: Four-day silent zen retreat with John (sensei), 22–25 October, in the Utrecht region. I couldn't open the page to confirm venue and price, so check before booking.

items.title: Silent museum mornings, Voorlinden
items.summary: Weekend mornings in silence, including Turrell's Skyspace. Meditation and museum in one.

items.title: EIC Accelerator: Deep Tech for Climate Adaptation
items.summary: 2026 challenge for startups on urban heat, climate-smart agriculture, water scarcity, and flood and coastal protection. Last full-application cut-off of 2026 is 4 November, 17:00 Brussels; short applications are open continuously.

items.title: Autumn food in Japan: chestnuts and new rice
items.summary: Kuri gohan (chestnut rice), roasted sweet potato and shinmai (new-crop rice) are naturally gluten-, dairy- and egg-free. Watch the soy sauce: regular shoyu contains wheat, so ask for tamari.

items.title: Register as an EU funding expert evaluator
items.summary: Paid remote work evaluating Horizon Europe, EIC and Innovation Fund proposals, including climate-adaptation calls: €450 per full day plus travel. Registration is open year-round.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto & Tin Drum: Kagami+
items.summary: Mixed-reality concert: Sakamoto appears as a 3D presence playing piano around you. Quiet and meditative, and it closes on 12 October.
items.why: Contemplative, immersive; you are in Japan until 9 Oct

items.title: teamLab Biovortex Kyoto
items.summary: teamLab's largest museum in Japan, 50+ works across 10,000 m², a short walk from Kyoto Station's Hachijō exit. Open 9:00–21:00 daily.

items.title: 2-day Zen retreat at Shunkō-in, 2–3 Oct
items.summary: Zazen, calligraphy, tea ceremony and shōjin ryōri, in English. Still open; the 29–30 Oct one is sold out. Temple food is vegan but often uses shoyu and fu (wheat), so tell them about gluten when booking.

items.title: Soy Milk Ramen Uno Yokiko
items.summary: Soy-milk ramen, gyoza and croquettes, reported 100% gluten-free and vegan, so no dairy or egg. Expect a queue; go early.

items.title: Celebrating the Icons of Art
items.summary: Voorlinden's 10th-birthday show pairs contemporary icons from the collection with their 20th-century predecessors. Combine with a silent morning and Turrell's Skyspace.
items.why: Voorlinden, Turrell, art in the dunes

items.title: Rui Chafes × Alberto Giacometti
items.summary: The Portuguese sculptor's dark, weightless steel forms in dialogue with Giacometti, in the museum dug into the Scheveningen dunes.

items.title: Van Gogh, all our paintings
items.summary: All 88 Van Goghs in the collection shown together for the first time since 1984. Pair it with the sculpture garden and an autumn walk in the Hoge Veluwe.

items.title: Turrell's largest Skyspace: As Seen Below – The Dome
items.summary: Opened at the summer solstice: the biggest Skyspace Turrell has built for a museum. A long drive or short flight, but a pilgrimage-grade Turrell.

items.title: GLOW light festival: Connect
items.summary: Eight evenings of light art along a walking route through Eindhoven, Oirschot, Best, Veldhoven, Helmond and Lieshout. Free.

items.title: Stille zondag, Zen.nl Den Haag
items.summary: Sunday morning 9:00–11:15: four 25-minute zazen rounds with kinhin, ending with tea. €15, needs prior zen experience and sign-up by email. Next dates 29 Nov and 20 Dec.

items.title: Weekend sesshin (Zen.nl Delft)
items.summary: Silent weekend of zazen, walking meditation and work practice, meals and lodging included (from €471). Ask about gluten, dairy, egg and oats.

items.title: OECD Forum on Green Finance and Investment
items.summary: The OECD's flagship green-finance forum, this year on investing for energy security, transition and resilience. You can join online from Japan.

items.title: Brussels Climate Week
items.summary: Four days with EU institutions, cities and investors; includes a Global Climate Finance Roundtable (Mon) and a Local Climate Finance Roundtable (Wed). Right after you land.

items.title: EU Mission Adaptation: Roster of Experts
items.summary: The Mission is building a roster of specialists to support regions and Mission projects, and explicitly asks for expertise in financing climate resilience. The first cohort started in September; applications stay open as it grows.

items.title: Northern lights: aim for the new moon around 8 March 2027
items.summary: Best odds this winter: early March in Rovaniemi (about half the nights clear) as the solar cycle winds down. Sooner option: the 9 November new moon in Tromsø, with direct flights from Schiphol from roughly €86–110 one-way if booked about six weeks out, i.e. now; cloud odds there are worse.
items.why: Bucket list: see the northern lights

items.title: Turrell's Open Sky at sunset, Chichu
items.summary: A 45-minute sunset session in Turrell's sky room inside Ando's buried museum, Friday and Saturday only; ¥3,700 including entry, 30 people per session.

items.title: Ando's Naoshima: New Museum of Art and Ando Museum
items.summary: Ando's tenth Naoshima building opened with Asian contemporary art (Cai Guo-Qiang, Aida Makoto); the Ando Museum nearby puts concrete and light inside a 100-year-old wooden house. Ferry from Uno.

items.title: Teshima Art Museum
items.summary: Nishizawa's concrete shell and Rei Naito's water drops among rice terraces: art that is almost only landscape, light and silence. ¥1,800.

items.title: Inujima Seirensho Art Museum
items.summary: A ruined copper refinery turned into a museum cooled by natural airflow, plus the island's Art House Project. Ferry from Hoden, east of Okayama city.

items.title: Private zazen at Hōfuku-ji, where Sesshū trained
items.summary: A Rinzai temple with a three-storey pagoda; they arrange an hour of zazen (two 20-minute sits, ¥1,000) at a time you choose. Book by phone, 0866-92-0024, probably in Japanese.

items.title: Okayama grape season: Pione and Muscat
items.summary: Peaches are over; now it's Pione, Shine Muscat and Muscat of Alexandria, with grape picking into mid-October. Fresh fruit is naturally safe; grape sweets are not a given.

items.title: Tsubame Kissashitsu (100% vegan)
items.summary: One-person vegan café with a Japanese set lunch (about ¥1,500), rated 5.0 on HappyCow; handy on a Kurashiki day.

items.title: Marisol
items.summary: A large retrospective of the Venezuelan-American sculptor, over 80 loans across the Depot's galleries; the Depot's big autumn show.

items.title: Reclining Figures
items.summary: The reclining figure in sculpture, in the dune museum at Scheveningen; ends two weeks after you're back.

items.title: Dutch Design Week: R.A.W.
items.summary: The 26th edition of the Netherlands' biggest design festival, with shows in old factories across Eindhoven.

items.title: Imagine Fantastic Film Festival: Ghost in the Feed
items.summary: Amsterdam's festival of science fiction and the fantastic; this year's theme is life inside the algorithm.

items.title: DAM-X: wing and windsurf weekend with gear tests
items.summary: Tenth edition: a Boardsports Market where you can test the newest wings and boards, plus clinics and freestyle shows. The weekend you're back.

items.title: Test wings on the beach at Versus Scheveningen
items.summary: Book Vayu wings and a Duotone Skybrid board to try at Scheveningen; Friday and Saturday without appointment, Mon–Thu by appointment.

items.title: Tokyo Sustainable Finance Forum
items.summary: FinCity.Tokyo's annual forum for asset owners, banks and regulators; free, in person or online with English interpretation. Register by 15 October.

items.title: Climate Adaptation and Resilience Seminar (Japan Weeks)
items.summary: One of the few events this autumn squarely on adaptation finance, during the FSA's Japan Weeks (26–30 Oct). Venue and registration not yet posted.

items.title: Nationaal Deltacongres
items.summary: The main Dutch event on a climate-resilient Netherlands and the Delta Programme revision. In-person is full: waitlist or join online.

items.title: Zazenkai with Jifu Roshi
items.place: Zen Centrum Rotterdam, Gebouw de Heuvel
items.summary: A full day of zazen, 10:00–16:30, €20. A forest zazenkai follows on 21 November.

items.title: Falling Leaves Sesshin
items.summary: Five-day silent sesshin at the Netherlands' largest zen temple, near the Wadden coast. Price on request.

items.title: Vosges forest hut from €9 a night
items.summary: A club hut in an old farmhouse in the Vosges forest, an hour's walk from Schirmeck station (train via Strasbourg), from €9; autumn colours now. Other huts nearby from €17. In Japan, Kōyasan temple stays in cedar forest are the equivalent.
items.why: Bucket list: Sleep in a beautiful mountain forest hut

items.title: €1 mountain houses still unassigned in the Piccole Dolomiti
items.place: Unione Montana Pasubio (Recoaro Terme, Valli del Pasubio, Posina)
items.summary: Only 13 of about 25 €1 houses were assigned in May; the rest are listed as unassigned and a new round is possible. Deed within 2 months, renovation within 3 years.
items.why: Bucket list: Own a 1€ house in Italy
flags: ask the Union about the unassigned houses

items.title: Okayama mountain houses from ¥1 million
items.summary: A Niimi house with land for ¥1M and a wooden house in Nishiawakura, a village that is 95% forest, for ¥2M. You're in the prefecture this week, and akiya banks like buyers to visit in person.
items.why: Bucket list: Own an affordable house in the mountains in a beautiful l forest
